# Scale accuracy verification (2026-11-24)

**Result: the printed scales are accurate.** Checked on PDFs generated by the app (A4 portrait 1:4000, A3 landscape 1:15000, A4 portrait custom 1:7300) by parsing the PDF content streams.

| Check | Expected | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Page size | A4 210 × 297 mm, A3 420 × 297 mm (landscape) | exactly that |
| Course legs (vector, 3 legs per PDF, 9 in total) | ground distance ÷ scale − symbol trims | difference < 0.0001 mm in all cases |
| Scale bar | 200 m at 1:4000 = 50.000 mm; 500 m at 1:15000 = 33.333 mm; 200 m at 1:7300 = 27.397 mm | identical |
| Map frame | page − 2 × 10 mm margin (190 × 277 mm; 400 × 277 mm) | identical |
| North line spacing | 50 mm | 50.000 mm |
| Map image (Mapant raster) | 190 × 277 mm at 10 mm, 150 dpi | 1122 × 1636 px placed as 190.000 × 277.000 mm |
| Raster ↔ vector alignment | every image pixel lands where `groundToPaper` puts the same ground point, one image pixel = metres·1000/scale mm | unit test, 4 scales × rotations (`src/core/core.test.ts`, "print accuracy") |

## What the scale is relative to
The map and the scale are defined in **TM35FIN grid metres**. The true (ellipsoidal) ground distance differs from the grid distance by the point scale factor of the projection. Across Finland (Hanko to Utsjoki, computed with the GRS80 ellipsoid) it is **0.99960 – 1.00043**, i.e. at most **0.04 mm per 100 mm of paper** (0.04 %). That is far below printing tolerance, so no correction is applied.

## Not covered
Real prints on paper (printer scaling must be set to 100 %, "actual size") and A3 at 300 dpi in Safari.

## Scale rules (implemented)
- Official scales stay the default: 1:3000, 1:4000, 1:7500, 1:10000, 1:15000.
- "Custom…" accepts any multiple of 100 from 1:100 to 1:50 000; other numbers are rounded to the nearest 100 and clamped (nothing smaller than 1:50 000). Paper size and orientation stay as chosen; only the ground area changes.
- The selected scale is always shown as a chip in the map toolbar, and in the PDF header.
- Saved scales and scales read from IOF XML are normalised with the same rule.
- Automatic generation is refused above 60 km² (e.g. A3 at 1:30000) with an explanatory message.
